section.title: Packaging
section.para: This document summarizes the process we follow to build the Agama packages.
The Agama packages are available in the systemsmanagement:Agama:Devel OBS project. These packages are automatically updated whenever the master branch is changed or when a new version is released.
You can find more details the automatic OBS synchronization in the obs_integration.md section.

The process to build each package is slightly different depending on the technology we are using. While the Ruby-based one (rubygem-agama-yast) is built as any other YaST package, the Agama server (agama), the CLI (agama-cli), and the web UI (agama-web-ui) rely on OBS source services.

section.title: Versioning policy
section.para: We have decided to follow a single number schema: 1, 2, 3, etc. However, if we need to release a hot-fix, we might use a dotted version (e.g., 2.1). Moreover, all the components share the same version number. Releasing a new version implies that all of them get the new number, no matter if they contain changes or not.

section.title: Bumping the version
section.para: In order to release a new version, we need to:

listitem.para: (cd service; bundle install) # Updates Gemfile.lock which is part of the repository
Add entries in the changes files. osc vc service/package osc vc rust/package osc vc web/package
Open a pull request to get these changes into the repository.

Once the pull request is merged, tag the repository with the proper version number. The processes to build the packages use this information to infer the version. You can set the tag with the rake tag command.
listitem.programlisting: # automatic version, use the current <major version> + 1 rake tag # manual version, useful for releasing a hot fix with a minor version rake tag[42.1]
listitem.para: You need to push the tag to the server manually, see the rake tag output.

section.para: After creating the tag on the server the GitHub Actions will publish the packages in the systemsmanagement:Agama:Devel project and create submit requests to openSUSE Factory.

section.title: Agama server, command-line and web-based user interface
section.para: You can find the current packages in OBS:

listitem.para: systemsmanagement:Agama:Devel/agama for the server and the command-line.

section.para: As mentioned before, those packages are built using a service-based approach. You need to make sure you installed the required OBS services: obs-service-obs_scm, osb-service-cargo, and obs-service-node_modules.
section.programlisting: zypper --non-interactive install --no-recommends \ obs-service-download_files obs-service-format_spec_file \ obs-service-obs_scm obs-service-cargo obs-service-node_modules
section.para: After checking out or branching the package, you need to run the following commands.
section.programlisting: osc service manualrun osc commit -m "Update sources" # or osc build
section.para: If you want to use a different Git branch, set another version, etc. just adapt the _service accordingly before running the osc service manualrun command.
The version number is inferred from the repository tags: it uses the latest tag and the offset of the latest commit respect such a tag. (e.g. 2.1+42).
You can read more about the overall approach of this package in the following article: Git work flows in the upcoming 2.7 release.
